subject: High cholesterol
object: having too much cholesterol, a fatty substance, in the blood.
source: NHS website: What is high cholesterol? - High cholesterol
source_quote: High cholesterol is when you have too much of a fatty substance called cholesterol in your blood.

subject: Dyslipidaemias
object: changes in the plasma lipid profile: raised total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol or triglycerides, or a low HDL cholesterol, or a combination of these.
source: Article: Merćep I, Strikić D, Slišković AM et al. New Therapeutic Approaches in Treatment of Dyslipidaemia—A Narrative Review. Pharmaceuticals 2022
source_quote: Dyslipidaemias, a crucial correctable predictive factor for coronary artery disease, are defined as alternations of the plasma lipid profile: increased levels of total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol or triglycerides, or a low plasma concentration of HDL cholesterol, or a combination of these features .

subject: A cholesterol test
object: total cholesterol, HDL ("good") cholesterol, and non-HDL cholesterol, which is the difference between total cholesterol and HDL.
source: NHS website: Cholesterol levels - High cholesterol
source_quote: A cholesterol test can measure: total cholesterol – the overall amount of cholesterol in your blood good cholesterol (called HDL) – this may make you less likely to have heart problems or a stroke non-HDL cholesterol – the difference between total cholesterol and HDL

subject: In hyperlipidaemia, LDL and HDL
object: the main lipoprotein carriers of the body's own cholesterol esters, and also carry smaller amounts of triglycerides, phospholipids and fat-soluble vitamins.
source: Article: Su L, Mittal R, Ramgobin D et al. Current Management Guidelines on Hyperlipidemia: The Silent Killer. Journal of Lipids 2021
source_quote: LDL and HDL are the primary lipoprotein transporters of endogenous cholesterol esters; however, they also carry lesser amounts of triglycerides, phospholipids, and fat soluble vitamins.

subject: In lipid metabolism relevant to hyperlipidaemia, HDL
object: cholesterol from peripheral cells to the liver and intestine.
source: Article: Su L, Mittal R, Ramgobin D et al. Current Management Guidelines on Hyperlipidemia: The Silent Killer. Journal of Lipids 2021
source_quote: For example, HDL serves to transport cholesterol from peripheral cells to the liver and intestine.

subject: In hypercholesterolaemia, raised cholesterol
object: plaque forming and building up in blood vessels, leading to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
source: Article: Su L, Mittal R, Ramgobin D et al. Current Management Guidelines on Hyperlipidemia: The Silent Killer. Journal of Lipids 2021
source_quote: Elevated cholesterol in the body can lead to plaque formation and buildup within vasculature, leading to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease as summarized in Figure 1 .

subject: In hypercholesterolaemia, LDL particles
object: pass through dysfunctional vascular endothelium and cause inflammation.
source: Article: Su L, Mittal R, Ramgobin D et al. Current Management Guidelines on Hyperlipidemia: The Silent Killer. Journal of Lipids 2021
source_quote: LDL particles can invade through dysfunctional vascular endothelium and cause subsequent inflammation.

subject: In hypercholesterolaemia, LDL entering the artery wall
object: monocytes infiltrating the subendothelial space, and macrophages taking up modified LDL particles and becoming foam cells, named for their high cholesterol load.
source: Article: Su L, Mittal R, Ramgobin D et al. Current Management Guidelines on Hyperlipidemia: The Silent Killer. Journal of Lipids 2021
source_quote: In response to the LDL invasion of the endothelium, monocytes infiltrate the subendothelial space . The macrophages take up the modified LDL particles and become foam cells, termed due to their high cholesterol load.

subject: Atherosclerotic plaque formation in hypercholesterolaemia
object: narrowing of the artery and plaque rupture, possibly causing ischaemic or thrombotic events.
source: Article: Su L, Mittal R, Ramgobin D et al. Current Management Guidelines on Hyperlipidemia: The Silent Killer. Journal of Lipids 2021
source_quote: The process of atherosclerosis plaque formation can lead to decreased arterial diameter and plaque rupture, potentially causing ischemic or thrombotic consequences.

subject: In hyperlipidaemia, LDL levels
object: the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, through both how high LDL cholesterol is and how long a person is exposed to it.
source: Article: Su L, Mittal R, Ramgobin D et al. Current Management Guidelines on Hyperlipidemia: The Silent Killer. Journal of Lipids 2021
source_quote: LDL levels have been causally associated with the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) through absolute magnitude and cumulative duration of LDL-C exposure .

subject: Hypercholesterolaemia, the most common form of dyslipidaemia,
object: raised LDL cholesterol, which has been shown to be an important cause of ischaemic heart disease and ischaemic stroke in both developed and developing countries.
source: Article: Merćep I, Strikić D, Slišković AM et al. New Therapeutic Approaches in Treatment of Dyslipidaemia—A Narrative Review. Pharmaceuticals 2022
source_quote: Hypercholesterolemia, the most common form of dyslipidemia, is associated with elevated LDL cholesterol levels, which have been shown to be an important causal factor for ischemic heart disease and ischemic stroke in both developed and developing countries .

subject: Too much cholesterol

source_quote: The most common phenotype IIb, familial combined hyperlipidaemia, consists of an abnormality in LDL and very-low-density lipoprotein (VLDL) cholesterol, affecting total cholesterol and/or triglycerides more than 90 percentile, and apolipoprotein more than 90 percentile.

subject: Ezetimibe
object: cholesterol absorption by blocking the NPC1L1 sterol transporter in the small intestine, which lowers cholesterol reaching the liver and increases clearance of cholesterol from the blood.
source: Article: Merćep I, Strikić D, Slišković AM et al. New Therapeutic Approaches in Treatment of Dyslipidaemia—A Narrative Review. Pharmaceuticals 2022
source_quote: Ezetimibe is a selective inhibitor of cholesterol absorption. The mechanism of action of ezetimibe is mediated by targeting the sterol transporter Neimann-Pick C1 Like 1 (NPC1L1), which is localized at the border cells in the small intestine. Binding to the transporter inhibits it and decreases the absorption of cholesterol, further decreasing cholesterol circulation through the liver, and finally increasing the clearance of cholesterol from blood .

subject: Ezetimibe
object: LDL cholesterol by 10 to 15% when used with statins, its effect mostly seen as co-therapy and varying with the statin.

subject: Bempedoic acid
object: ATP citrate lyase, an enzyme upstream of HMG-CoA reductase, which prevents cholesterol synthesis and indirectly increases LDL receptors, increasing LDL clearance.
source: Article: Merćep I, Strikić D, Slišković AM et al. New Therapeutic Approaches in Treatment of Dyslipidaemia—A Narrative Review. Pharmaceuticals 2022
source_quote: Bempedoic acid is an adenosine triphosphate (ATP) citrate lyase inhibitor that inhibits cholesterol biosynthesis and increases LDL receptor expression. ATP citrate lyase is an enzyme upstream of HMG-CoA reductase in the biochemical cholesterol synthesis pathway. Inhibition of ATP citrate lyase prevents endogenous cholesterol synthesis and indirectly increases the expression of LDL receptors, thereby increasing the clearance of LDL cholesterol .

subject: Alirocumab and evolocumab (PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies)
object: PCSK9 binding to the liver's LDL receptors, which PCSK9 otherwise sends for degradation, so more LDL receptors are recycled and more LDL cholesterol is taken up from the blood.
source: Article: Merćep I, Strikić D, Slišković AM et al. New Therapeutic Approaches in Treatment of Dyslipidaemia—A Narrative Review. Pharmaceuticals 2022
source_quote: PCSK9 plays an important role in LDL receptor downregulation. LDL receptors are found on hepatocytes and play a role in the removal of circulating LDL cholesterol from blood. When the PCSK9 protein binds to the LDL receptor, it starts the process of degrading the receptor, thus increasing LDL cholesterol levels. The monoclonal antibodies alirocumab and evolocumab inhibit PCSK9 binding to LDL receptors, increase recycling of LDL receptors, and indirectly lower circulating LDL cholesterol levels by increasing LDL cholesterol uptake .

subject: Inclisiran
object: a small interfering RNA that cuts PCSK9 messenger RNA, reducing PCSK9 production, which upregulates LDL receptors and lowers circulating LDL cholesterol.
source: Article: Merćep I, Strikić D, Slišković AM et al. New Therapeutic Approaches in Treatment of Dyslipidaemia—A Narrative Review. Pharmaceuticals 2022
source_quote: It is a small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) that targets PCSK9. Inclisiran, an siRNA, interferes with the translation of PCSK9 by cleaving messenger RNA, thereby decreasing PCSK9 production. The absence of PCSK9 results in the upregulation of LDL receptors and, consequently, lowers the circulating level of LDL cholesterol .

subject: ApoC-III
object: a target for a new class of drugs meant to lower triglycerides, and indirectly to prevent cardiovascular events and pancreatitis in people with hypertriglyceridaemia.

source_quote: As such, apoC-III is a target for a new class of drugs aimed to lower triglyceride levels and indirectly preventing cardiovascular incidents and pancreatitis episodes in patients with hypertriglyceridemia.

subject: Raised lipoprotein(a)
object: an independent risk factor for atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease; Lp(a) is an LDL cholesterol variant that contains apolipoprotein(a).

subject: Hypercholesterolaemia
relation: has become less common in high-income countries (especially Europe and North America)

source_quote: Lifestyle changes, improvements in dietary habits and increased use of lipid-lowering drugs, in part because of their lower cost as most statins are available in generic forms, have led to a decrease in the prevalence of hypercholesterolemia and consequently, a reduction in mean plasma cholesterol levels in high-income countries (especially in Europe and North America) .
